thread:
sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: streaming-tail p99 > 1200ms in eu-west-2 for 5m. Auto-threshold triggered. Potential packet loss / TLS handshake noise. Paging oncall @oncall-alex @jess :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: i'm on it, looking at the streamer dashboards and egress metrics. p95 is OK but p99 and tail for streaming sessions spike. link: https://dashboards.internal/re/streams?region=eu-west-2

jess: grabbing nets stats now. seeing SYN retransmit rate increase and a jump in conntrack drops on nat-gw-eu2-azc. running `ssh nat-gw-eu2 sudo ss -s`

oncall-alex: paste results?

jess: output:

```
Total: 12345 (kernel 12345)
TCP: 20000 (established 15000, closed 3000, orphaned 0, synrecv 500, timewait 2500)
TCP retrans: 1100 (retransmits due to sacked?)

conntrack entries: 65535/65535 used
conntrack dropped: 412
```

maria-net: yep, conntrack at capacity on that NAT node. ephemeral port exhaustion pattern too. I also see elevated SNAT port allocation churn in cloud telemetry. next step: either increase SNAT pool size or steer traffic off azc.

oncall-alex: how bad is customer impact? @customer-ops any reports?

customer-ops: getting reports from 3 tenants. most severe: acme-chat streaming sessions report stall and reconnects, seeing ~8% error rate in EU sessions. flagging customer-facing comms. no billing impact yet, P2.

kevin-eng: can we flip a route table or scale NAT? we have reserved spare NAT instances in eu-west-2-azb.

jess: i'm testing a short-term mitigation: update LB routing to prefer azb/backends and disable azc for new stream sessions. will run a canary to 5% first. config snippet:

```hcl
resource "route_update" "steer_azb" {
  region = "eu-west-2"
  avoid_az = "azc"
  percent = 95
}
```

oncall-alex: do it. @pete-sre please watch conntrack counters while we roll.

pete-sre: watching. running `watch -n 2 "sudo conntrack -L | wc -l"` on nat-gw-eu2-azc and nat-gw-eu2-azb

(devops-bot): automation: created route-update change request CR-298712, will apply in 30s with canary 5% -> 25% -> 95% rollout.

jess: applied 5% canary -> azb. initial telemetry: new sessions landing on azb, conntrack usage on azc still high but not increasing. p99 for canary sessions ~240ms.

oncall-alex: good. continue rollout to 25%. keep original node in place for existing sessions.

(customer-ops): update: acme-chat saw reconnects drop from 8% to 1.6% for new sessions after canary. older sessions still affected until session refresh.

jess: rolled to 95% now. observing nat-gw-eu2-azc conntrack fall from 65535 -> 32000 over 3 minutes. SYN retransmit rate decreasing. p99 across region dropped to ~220ms.

maria-net: adding follow-up: create alert to warn at conntrack >= 80% and automated SNAT pool expansion as runbook. also propose permanent traffic steering rule during peak for that AZ until we repro the root cause.

oncall-alex: quick root cause hypotheses: increased short-lived connections from a crawler or customer job pinned to azc that generated ephemeral port churn. we saw no infra CPU or NIC errors. need packet captures to confirm.
